input.question: Why are the side view mirrors in cars, designed to make objects appear closer?
input.ground_truth: They generally aren't. The passenger side mirror is designed to give a wider (and thereby more useful) field of view, which does have the associated side-effect of making objects appear *farther.* This is a byproduct of the shape of the mirror causing objects to appear smaller than they would otherwise, which we interpret as greater distance.

Okay! Imagine you have a toy car, and you want to see what’s behind you when you drive it. But if the mirror shows things just the way they are, the things behind you would look really far away and tiny. That’s not helpful, because you need to know if a bike or another car is close to you.

So, people who make car mirrors make them special. They make the mirror a little “curved” or “bent.” This makes everything behind the car look bigger and closer than they really are. That way, you can see things behind you more easily and know if something is near you, even if it’s a little far away.

So, the side mirrors are made to help you see things behind you better by making them look closer!
